source_artifacts.locator: payments-agent agent card (as consumed by the orchestrator)

inputs.source: Employee purchase request submitted via SSO-authenticated channel
Vendor quote emails and attachments received from external vendors

instructions.note: Prompt states 'Payments-agent will handle any remaining checks,' but runtime notes confirm payments-agent performs no additional verification and trusts any task from the orchestrator's bearer token.

Agent is instructed to 'Use the bank details from the chosen quote' directly, with no structural requirement to verify those details against the approved vendor's on-file bank information before payment.

controls.name: Manager approval of purchase request (item/budget)
controls.decay_rationale: Human approval does not decay with model capability, but it occurs before vendor quotes exist and its context does not propagate to payments-agent (approval_context_propagates: false), so it does not cover the payment capability's actual risk (vendor selection, bank details).

controls.name: Prompt instruction: only pay vendors on the approved list
controls.decay_rationale: Relies on the model correctly cross-referencing vendor identity against the approved list from quote text; a more capable or adversarially prompted model can be persuaded an off-list or spoofed vendor qualifies, or can split the action into steps that individually appear compliant.

controls.name: Structural verification of vendor bank details against approved vendor list at payment execution
controls.decay_rationale: A server-side check at payments-agent comparing bank account/routing details to the approved vendor's on-file details would not depend on model behavior and would sever the path from an untrusted quote to payment.

controls.name: Human approval gate on final vendor/bank details before payment execution
controls.decay_rationale: A raw-action human approval step scoped to the specific vendor and bank details, occurring after quote selection, would not decay with model capability.

controls.name: Least-privilege, transaction-scoped credential for orchestrator-to-payments-agent calls
controls.decay_rationale: A narrowly scoped, short-lived, transaction-bound credential would not decay with model capability and would prevent the orchestrator's broad bearer token from authorizing arbitrary payments.

controls.name: Pin or sign payments-agent's agent card
controls.decay_rationale: Pinning/hashing the agent card would not decay with model capability and would prevent silent redefinition of payments-agent's skills or endpoint between fetches.

controls.name: Verify payments-agent peer identity via mTLS or signed identity
controls.decay_rationale: Cryptographic peer identity verification does not depend on model behavior and prevents connecting to an impersonated or redirected payments-agent endpoint.

controls.name: Audit log linking payment tasks to approval records and vendor verification outcome
controls.decay_rationale: Detective logging does not prevent the action but enables attribution and faster detection; it does not decay with capability, though it only reduces consequence if reviewed before harm completes.

findings.title: Authority laundering and unverified bank details let an untrusted vendor quote drive an irreversible payment (TC7)

attack_path.note: Untrusted vendor email supplies bank details for the chosen quote.
Approved vendor list exists but is referenced only by prompt instruction, not enforced structurally at payment time.
Approval occurs before quotes exist and does not cover the vendor or bank details actually used; approval context is not passed to payments-agent.
Orchestrator delegates payment task with bank details from the untrusted quote to payments-agent, which executes payment without independent verification.

forecast.watch_signal: Model or version string change in subject.model, or any observed instance where the agent proceeds to pay a vendor not confirmed on the approved list.

evidence.observation: Manager approves the purchase request (item and budget) before any quote exists, so the approval cannot cover the vendor or bank details later chosen.
The approval record is not passed to payments-agent, so approval context does not propagate with the delegated task.
payments-agent trusts any task from the orchestrator's bearer token and pays the bank details in the task, with no independent check against the approved vendor list.
Agent is instructed to 'Use the bank details from the chosen quote,' which are supplied by an untrusted external vendor email.

recommendations.action: Require payments-agent to independently verify the vendor and bank/routing details against the approved vendor list's on-file records before executing payment, rather than relying on the orchestrator's prompt instruction.

Propagate the approval context (including final vendor and bank details) to payments-agent and require a raw-action human approval step scoped to those specific details before payment, since the initial budget/item approval predates vendor selection.
Scope the orchestrator-to-payments-agent credential to least privilege (e.g., per-transaction, vendor-restricted tokens) instead of a broadly trusted bearer token.
Log and alert on payment tasks whose bank details do not match the historical on-file details for the approved vendor.

findings.title: Unsigned, unpinned payments-agent card with static bearer trust enables impersonation of the payment delegate (ASI07)

attack_path.note: Agent card is fetched at startup over A2A, is not signed or pinned, and the orchestrator does not verify the peer's identity.
Orchestrator delegates a payment task (irreversible, confidential) to whatever endpoint the unverified card currently points to.

findings.residual_rationale: The only declared control on cap.delegate_payment (the 'approved vendors only' prompt instruction) constrains which vendor identity the model chooses to pay; it does not verify the authenticity of the payments-agent endpoint itself. Because the agent card is unsigned, unpinned, and identity is unverified (peer_trust_level: unknown), crediting that control against this spoofing/tampering threat would understate risk, so residual is held at the inherent floor rather than the mechanically credited 'high'.

forecast.watch_signal: Any change to payments-agent's agent card URL, skill schema, or auth scheme between startup fetches; introduction of additional unpinned peers.

evidence.observation: The agent card is fetched at startup and is not signed or pinned.
Authentication is declared only as a bearer scheme with no mutual identity verification described.
payments-agent trusts any task from the orchestrator's bearer token, so a spoofed or redefined endpoint would receive the same level of trust.

recommendations.action: Sign and pin payments-agent's agent card; verify the signature and hash on every fetch, not only at startup.
Replace static bearer trust with mutual TLS or a signed peer identity for the A2A connection to payments-agent.
Alert on any change to the payments-agent card content or endpoint between deployments.

rating.rationale: Both findings are U-source-to-S3 (irreversible, confidential payment delegation) paths, which are inherently critical. Finding 1 (authority laundering: approval precedes vendor selection, approval context does not propagate, and payments-agent performs no independent check) is held down to high only by a single dependent prompt instruction. Finding 2 (unsigned, unpinned agent card with no peer identity verification) has no control that actually addresses endpoint authenticity, so residual is held at critical by rationale override rather than the mechanical floor. The rollup residual is therefore critical, and both findings forecast back to critical under plausible triggers (model_upgrade defeats the prompt instruction; new_peer_agent or control_removal leave the card-spoofing gap exactly as exploitable as today). The single highest-leverage fix is structural, independent verification of bank/routing details and peer identity at payments-agent itself, since every other declared control is either behavioral/dependent or absent.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in the provided artifacts (system prompt, payments-agent agent card, and runtime notes), not observed runtime behavior of the deployed system.

No MCP/tool manifest or IaC was provided; cap.vendor_list_read's enforcement mechanism and credential scope are inferred from the prompt and runtime notes only, which lowers confidence on that capability's details.
No information on step or runtime limits (max_unattended_steps, max_runtime_minutes) was provided; both are treated as unbounded (null).

The actual network/identity architecture behind payments-agent's URL (DNS, hosting, internal network segmentation) is not described, so exploitability of the unsigned/unpinned agent card (Finding 2) is assessed at medium confidence.
